questions.question: Which of the following is a common visual or physical indicator that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: A change in colour, bubbling, or a change of temperature
A change in the shape of a container without any temperature change
A substance dissolving completely to make a transparent solution
A liquid turning into a gas at its boiling point

questions.question: What occurs at the atomic level during a chemical reaction?
options: Atoms are destroyed and entirely new atoms are created
Atoms rearrange themselves to form new substances
Atoms melt together to form one giant super-atom
Atoms change their element type to become different elements

questions.question: Which statement generally describes the reversibility of chemical reactions?
options: They are easily reversed by cooling down the products
They can always be reversed by adding water
They are generally irreversible
They can be reversed by physical filtering

questions.question: What three components are required to start a combustion reaction?
options: Fuel, carbon dioxide, and water
Fuel, nitrogen, and a catalyst
Fuel, oxygen, and an initial source of energy like heat
Carbon dioxide, water, and electricity

questions.question: Under what conditions is water often formed as a product in a chemical reaction?
options: If oxygen and hydrogen atoms are present in the reactants
Only when a metal reacts with an acid
If carbon and nitrogen atoms are present in the reactants
When any substance is heated above 100 degrees Celsius

questions.question: What characterizes a chemical decomposition reaction?
options: Two elements combining to form a single compound
A single compound breaking down into two or more products
A solid dissolving into a liquid solvent
Two solutions mixing to form an insoluble solid

questions.question: What products typically form when metal carbonates decompose upon heating?
options: Metal oxides and carbon dioxide gas
Metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas
Pure metals and oxygen gas
Metal chlorides and water

questions.question: What is the term for a chemical reaction in which a substance combines with oxygen?
options: Reduction
Decomposition
Precipitation
Oxidation

questions.question: Which of the following pairs are both examples of oxidation reactions?
options: Combustion and rusting
Melting and evaporation
Neutralisation and filtration
Thermal decomposition and dissolving

questions.question: What defines a precipitation reaction when two solutions are mixed together?
options: The release of a large amount of flammable gas
The formation of an insoluble solid
A rapid increase in temperature without any state change
The complete neutralisation of an acid and alkali

questions.question: How are precipitation reactions practically applied in water treatment?
options: To heat the water up to its boiling point quickly
To add oxygen gas to make the water taste fresher
To remove unwanted substances from water by forming solids that can be filtered
To dissolve large organic waste particles into smaller molecules

questions.question: How does the total mass of the products in a chemical reaction compare to the total mass of the reactants?
options: The mass of the products is always less because some mass is converted to energy
The mass of the products is always greater because new atoms are made
The mass of the products is the same as the mass of the reactants
The mass of the products depends entirely on whether a gas was released

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using word equations in chemistry?
options: To calculate the exact masses of the reacting chemicals
To provide a simple way of describing chemical reactions
To list the physical states of all reactants and products
To show the microscopic arrangement of chemical bonds

questions.question: What do chemical equations represent about a chemical reaction?
options: The time taken for the reaction to go to completion
The temperature change that occurs during the reaction
How the atoms in the reactants rearrange to form the products
The cost and availability of the reactants used

questions.question: In a chemical equation, what does the arrow represent?
options: "Equals the mass of"
"Changes into"
"Is reversible with"
"Dissolves in"
